ANIMATION_MODEL_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.trigger: Operator: 'dig deeper to get your answer' -- resolving whether terrain animation exists at all, previously flagged as the row's one evidence-free sub-domain.
ANIMATION_MODEL_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.method_pass_1: Isolated Interpreter instance (/tmp/dsrepro-e01-anim-20260803, port 23645): loaded three scenes (level01.sav scene 1, level02.sav scene 3, canyon_bug.sav scene 6), idled each with zero input, snapshotted full 1024x512 VRAM via gpu.readVramRect at ~90-frame intervals, diffed per 32x32 cell. Churn classified: (a) the double-buffered framebuffer pair -- mirrored cell blocks exactly 512 apart in x, whose per-scene size tracks how much on-screen MOTION the idle scene has (scene 3 nearly still: 29 cells; LEVEL01 with wandering enemies: 111; Cliffside settling after load: 257 then 72/59); (b) a relocating streaming-upload signature -- the same 64x128 two-column cell shape at a DIFFERENT x per level (L01/canyon at x=640-704, scene 3 at x=512-576) = per-frame character/effect texture streaming, not terrain; (c) scattered y>=448 cells = CLUT/HUD rows.
ANIMATION_MODEL_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.method_pass_2_level01_focused: Snapshotted only the LEVEL01 terrain-page band (VRAM 0..768 x 0..256, pages 0-11 per the committed page<->chunk map) 5 times at 30-frame intervals, hashing every 32x32 cell: 187/192 cells (97.4%) byte-stable. The 4 changing page-10 cells show ALL-DISTINCT contents (forward streaming -- the signature from pass 1, which happens to sit inside the page band). Exactly ONE cell CYCLES: (256,32) in page 4, 4 distinct contents with a repeat over 5 snapshots -- a genuine flipbook.
ANIMATION_MODEL_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.offline_uv_join: Joined the cycling cell against the extractor's LEVEL01 decode (per-face texpage chunk + UVs): the tile (chunk 4, 4bpp texels u<128, 32<=v<64) is sampled by exactly 52 faces -- ALL inside ONE dedicated payload, 'fcn.80010000 payload @0x4c1a4', classification scenery_surface, whose faces repeatedly map the same 64x64-texel rect. No other mesh touches the tile (268 chunk-4 faces total).
ANIMATION_MODEL_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.conclusion: Terrain/scenery animation EXISTS in exactly one identified form: flipbook tile RE-UPLOAD (VRAM texture replacement on a cycle) driving a single dedicated scenery-surface payload -- a water-like animated surface. All other terrain texture content is byte-stable while idling, and no palette-cycling (CLUT animation) was observed in the page band. The row's animation sub-domain moves from 'no evidence either way' to a precise, narrow mechanism.
ANIMATION_MODEL_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.hypothesis_flagged_not_traced: The uploader is plausibly the ALREADY-Canon 0x22-chunk animation-strip pipeline (the training-word letter system: 16-frame tile-keyed strips, committed training-word-native-pipeline Canon) reused for scenery tiles -- consistent shape (small tile, frame strip, periodic upload), but the actual upload call site/PC and the strip's disc source were NOT traced this pass.
